mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and input costs rise.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% over three months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase over 3 months and UNRATE stable or decrease
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over six months signals rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over two consecutive quarters signals an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
